7 انبثق It (water) had vent; or it poured out, or flowed forth: (S, Msb, * K:) or it ran, or flowed, of itself, without the breaking through of a dam or the like. (Mgh.) [For اِنْفَجَرَ, in the S, Golius appears to have found اِنْفَرَجَ, which is a mistake. ―
-b2- The Christians, as Golius has observed, use this verb to denote the procession of the Holy Spirit.] ―
-b3- انبثق السَّيْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ (tropical:) The torrent came upon them without their expecting it, or thinking it. (K, * TA.) And المَآءُ عَلَيْهِمْ ↓ بَثَقَ (assumed tropical:) The water came upon them. (TA.) ―
-b4- انبثق عَلَيْهِمْ بِالكِلَامِ (tropical:) He came upon them with speech without their expecting it. (K, * TA.) ―
-b5- انبثقت الأَرْضُ (tropical:) The land became abundant in herbage, or fruitful. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
